why: The student doesn't give the output or say when the loop stops. Instead they correctly claim that a changed program, which assigns the boolean straight to isDone instead of using the if, behaves the same, so this is reasoning about code that isn't given.

concepts.quote: isDone = (i % 5 == 0); would do the same as the if.
concepts.why: This is correct new code: isDone is always false while the loop is running, so assigning the test result directly gives the same output, 1 4 7 10, and stops at the same point as the if.
It correctly stores the value of a boolean expression in isDone, and this new statement replaces the if.
The answer reuses i % 5 but says nothing about what it works out to.
The answer says nothing about the loop's && condition.
